extracted.intended_audience: education researchers, K-12 administrators, and teacher professional-development planners interested in teacher grant writing
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based study and guidance about factors that motivate K-12 teachers to write grants, obstacles they encounter, and support/staff-development needs to increase successful grantseeking and grant management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved Student Learning (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making a contribution to improved student learning — measured as a motivating factor for writing a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a 4-point scale for motivating factors (4 = strong motivator, 3 = average motivator, 2 = not a motivator, 1 = does not apply). In this study 94% of teachers identified improved student learning as a strong motivator; use this item to evaluate intrinsic, student-centered motivation for grant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Needed Equipment (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having the resources to acquire badly needed equipment — a motivating factor for grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 4-point motivator scale. In this study 91% rated this as a strong motivator; applies to proposals aimed at procuring classroom materials/technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction in Obtaining Funding / Personal Satisfaction (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfaction in obtaining grant funding / personal satisfaction in having a grant funded — considered a motivator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated 4-1 on motivator scale. In this sample 67% identified satisfaction as an average or strong motivator; useful to assess personal reward/intrinsic motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building Professional Reputation (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Building a personal professional reputation as a successful grant writer — a potential motivating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated with the same 4-point motivator scale; evaluates career/professional recognition motives distinct from institutional recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition from the School District / Administration (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaining recognition from the school district and/or school administration as a motivator to write grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4-point motivator scale. In this study recognition was less often a motivator overall (only 26% average/strong), but differences by prior funding level were significant: teachers with $1000–$5000 prior funding rated district recognition as a greater motivator than those with <$1000 (p < .05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Teacher Load to Work on Grants (motivating factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced teacher workload to permit time for grant-writing activities — included as a motivator item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4-point motivator scale; captures whether release time or workload reduction motivates engagement in grant projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Knowledge of Funding Opportunities (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers' lack of knowledge of grant funding sources — identified as an obstacle to grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a 5-point obstacle scale (5 = extreme obstacle, 4 = great, 3 = medium, 2 = low, 1 = not an obstacle). In this study 79% rated this as an extreme/great/average obstacle; teachers with <$1000 prior funding perceived this as a greater obstacle than teachers with >$5000 (p < .05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Budgeting and Account Management Knowledge (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of knowledge of budgeting and account management for grants — a practical obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point obstacle scale. Significant group differences found: teachers with <$1000 prior funding perceived budgeting knowledge as a greater obstacle compared to teachers with >$5000 (One-way ANOVA, p < .05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Encouragement from School Administration (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived lack of encouragement from the school district or administration to pursue grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point obstacle scale. In this sample most teachers rated lack of encouragement as a low/no obstacle (81%); contrasts with earlier studies. Use to assess institutional climate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Technical Assistance in Writing Competitive Proposals (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of access to technical assistance for proposal development — an obstacle to successful grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point obstacle scale. 56% reported technical assistance as an extreme to average obstacle; teachers with <$1000 prior funding perceived this as a greater obstacle than teachers with >$5000 (p < .01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems with School District Business Office (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulties in dealing with the district business office when managing grants — included as an obstacle item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point obstacle scale. Captures administrative/financial management barriers imposed by district procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased Workload Possibly Preventing Future Grant Writing (obstacle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which increased workload from grant-related activities would discourage future grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point obstacle scale including an option indicating workload would prevent future grant writing; assesses sustainability of teacher engagement given workload burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Office Identification of Available Funding Sources (support frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often support personnel in central office identify available funding sources for teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point frequency scale (5 = Very Frequently, 4 = Frequently, 3 = Occasionally, 2 = Rarely, 1 = Never). Use to evaluate central-office proactive support in matching teachers to opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Identification of Available Funding Sources (support frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often the principal identifies available funding sources to teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point frequency scale. Measures school-level administrative support for grant seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Development Received Prior to Writing Grant (adequacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher-rated adequacy of staff development/training received before writing the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point adequacy scale (5 = very adequate, 4 = adequate, 3 = less than adequate, 2 = inadequate, 1 = no training). In this study 76% rated prior training as adequate or greater; nevertheless 99% said continued staff development was needed to support future grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty Managing a Grant through School District (management difficulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher-rated difficulty of managing an awarded grant through district processes once funding was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5-point difficulty scale (5 = very easy, 4 = easy, 3 = somewhat difficult, 2 = very difficult, 1 = so difficult as to prevent future grant writing, 0 = Does not apply). Teachers with larger prior funding (>$1000) perceived management difficulties as a greater obstacle than teachers with <$1000 (p < .01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness / Essential Nature of Continued Support for Grant Writing and Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived helpfulness of continued support for grant writing and grant management to sustain future grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4-point helpfulness scale (4 = Essential for continued grant writing, 3 = Very Helpful, 2 = Helpful, 1 = Not helpful). Use to prioritize ongoing supports and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years of Teaching (grouping variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of years the teacher has been teaching — used as an independent grouping variable to examine differences in motivators/obstacles/support needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorized (e.g., <1, 1 year, 2–5, 6–10, >10). Included as an independent variable in One-Way ANOVA comparisons; useful to tailor staff development to career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Grants Written (grouping variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency category of how many grants a teacher has submitted (1, 2–4, 5–9, 10–12, etc.) — used as an independent grouping variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in analyses (ANOVA, correlations). A significant positive correlation was found between number of grants written and level of prior grant funding (p < .01), indicating experience predicts funding success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Level Achieved in Previous Grants (grouping variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total dollar amount of previous grant funding obtained by a teacher (categories include Unfunded, $500–$1,000, $1,000–$5,000, $5,000–$10,000, etc.) — used as the primary independent variable distinguishing groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect differences in perceived motivators, obstacles and support needs (One-Way ANOVA). Findings: teachers with <$1000 prior funding perceive knowledge, budgeting and technical assistance as greater obstacles; mid-range ($1000–$5000) value recognition more; high funding (> $5000) report management difficulties as larger obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Likert-style Scales and One-way ANOVA / Correlation Analysis (measurement & analysis approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionnaire uses multiple Likert-style scales to measure motivators, obstacles, and support needs; group differences analyzed via One-Way ANOVA and relationships tested with correlations/t-tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies measurement and statistical approach (item-level Likert scales, grouping by years/number/funding, ANOVA to compare groups, two-tailed t-test/correlation to test relationships). Guidance for replication or program evaluation: employ similar item wording/scales and statistical tests to compare teacher subgroups and assess intervention effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic/Administrative Supports (recommended actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and programmatic measures that facilitate teacher grant writing: train staff and administrators as proposal writers, develop district grant-writing procedures, reduce teaching loads when necessary, provide technical assistance and central-office identification of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not measured as scales, the paper recommends these concrete supports based on findings and prior literature (Brown & Schenck, Monahan). Use these as implementation criteria when designing teacher grant-support programs.
